rationale: The pain is real — a broken concurrency layer on self-hosted LLM inference directly blocks production batch workloads and wastes developer time. However, the buyers are technical developers and small engineering teams who expect to self-solve infrastructure problems or use open-source fixes; willingness to pay for a managed proxy/scheduler tool is unvalidated and likely low in this audience. More decisively, building a reliable local inference concurrency proxy requires deep systems/networking work that goes well beyond Claude + a landing page, and ongoing delivery requires per-deployment support that is inherently hands-on. Not viable for this factory.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for this factory. A local inference concurrency proxy is a systems-level product (thread pools, request queuing, inter-process communication) that cannot be built with Claude + prompts + Stripe. The target buyers (self-hosting developers) also have a strong bias toward open-source self-service and would be unlikely to pay for a managed wrapper. Drop.
